dedupe_keys.name: epa analysis of lithium ion battery fires in waste management and recycling 245 fires 2013 to 2020

description: This report compiles fires caused by lithium-ion and lithium metal batteries in the US waste management process. It was written by Phoebe O'Connor and Patrick Wise of the US Environmental Protection Agency's Office of Resource Conservation and Recovery and published in July 2021 as report EPA 530-R-21-002. The authors searched public information, mostly local news, and interviewed industry experts, and found 64 facilities that had 245 fires caused or likely caused by batteries between 2013 and 2020, in 28 states and all 10 EPA regions. Facilities include materials recovery facilities, collection trucks, landfills, transfer stations and electronics recyclers; each is described with its fires and impacts, grouped as injuries, external emergency response, service disruption and monetary loss. Of the materials recovery facilities, 78 percent had called emergency responders at least once, against 40 percent of landfills. The report is free to download online as a PDF and, as a US federal work, is in the public domain. Caveats: the list covers only fires that reached the news, which the authors say is a fraction of the total, and it is not maintained. Simulation uses: fire frequencies and impact types for waste facility disruption and hazard models. Related records: the Fire Rover monthly fire reports (data-fire-rover-waste-recycling-facility-fire-reports) continue the count across all causes.
